portfolio.name: Personal Portfolio
portfolio.description: Is this a temporal loop? You are already here! 😄
portfolio.overview: This repository contains a production-ready Next.js portfolio with a modular component structure, custom design tokens, and accessibility-focused UI. It includes a homepage with hero, projects, education and contact sections, plus dedicated project pages and a minimal CMS-like data structure driven by TypeScript types.
keyFeatures: Server and client components where appropriate (app router structure)
Type-safe content model for projects and metadata
Responsive layout and modern UI tokens (dark + light mode)
Optimized images and metadata for social sharing
decisions: Use Next.js App Router for a clear separation between server and client rendering
TypeScript-first data shapes so project pages are strongly typed and editor-friendly
Tailwind for rapid, consistent styling and small bundle size
impact: Smaller time-to-market for new content because projects are simple data objects
Improved UX on mobile and desktop with optimized images and semantic markup
Easier maintenance thanks to component-driven architecture

radio-seeker.name: Radio Seeker
radio-seeker.description: A web application that lets users search, add, edit, remove, and listen to online radio stations. With a simple, user-friendly interface and practical features, users can easily manage their favorite radio stations.
radio-seeker.overview: Radio Seeker is a Next.js (v14.2.3) application built with JavaScript that emphasizes usability and accessibility. The UI is implemented with Radix UI and shadcn/ui and styled with Tailwind CSS. Forms and validation are handled with react-hook-form, @hookform/resolvers, and Zod, while notifications use Sonner. The app supports station search, inline playback, local persistence of favorites (localStorage), and quick editing. Architecturally, Next.js was chosen for hybrid routing and SSG/SSR where appropriate, keeping a lean bundle and a fast developer experience.
keyFeatures: Search stations by name or metadata
Add, edit and remove stations from a persisted list
Inline audio player with play/pause and basic controls
Persist favorites locally with optional backend sync
Accessible, component-driven UI built with Radix + shadcn/ui
decisions: Choose Next.js for hybrid routing and SSG/SSR where appropriate
Use Radix UI + shadcn/ui to build accessible, composable components
Use react-hook-form + Zod for resilient form handling and validation
Persist favorites in localStorage for offline-first UX and optional sync
Centralize audio playback in a shared component to avoid concurrent streams
impact: Demonstrates reliable inline audio playback and media controls
Showcases accessible, component-driven UI patterns (Radix + shadcn)
Provides a practical example of client-side persistence and CRUD flows
Good technical talking point for form validation and UX trade-offs

weather98.name: Weather98
weather98.description: Compact weather dashboard with a nostalgic Windows 98 aesthetic. Integrates OpenWeather One Call 3.0, provides geolocation and search, short-term forecasts, local caching, and resilient error handling.
weather98.overview: Weather98 pairs a playful retro UI with pragmatic engineering: Vite + React for a snappy dev experience, TypeScript for safer code, Axios for API requests, and local caching to limit network calls. Features include current conditions, a 3-day forecast, city search with geolocation fallback, and graceful handling of rate limits and missing data.
keyFeatures: Search by city and optional geolocation fallback
Network error handling and user-friendly messages
Language and unit preferences settable and persisted
decisions: Cache results for a short TTL to improve UX and stay within API rate limits
Abstract API client so swapping providers is straightforward
Prioritize clear micro-interactions to surface loading and error states
impact: Shows competency integrating third-party APIs and handling edge cases
Practical pattern for caching and error-handling in small apps
Great interview talking point for trade-offs when designing API-driven UI

burger-app.name: Burger App
burger-app.description: Interactive burger menu app with component-driven UI and state management for assembling orders.
burger-app.overview: A small single-page application that demonstrates modular component design, dynamic state for building orders and a lightweight UI system. The app focuses on composition patterns and predictable state updates to simulate an ordering flow.
keyFeatures: Composable UI components for burger ingredients
Local state management for cart/build flow
decisions: Favor small, focused components so the ordering flow is easy to reason about
Keep state local where possible to avoid unnecessary global complexity
Use Tailwind to iterate quickly on UI without a large stylesheet
impact: Clear demonstration of component composition and state-driven UI
Lightweight bundle suitable for quick prototypes
Easy to fork and adapt as a UI pattern library example

faq-1.question: What technologies do you specialize in?
faq-1.answer: I specialize in React, Next.js (App Router), React Native (Expo), TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. I also work with state management (Zustand, Redux), testing (Jest, React Testing Library), and modern build/CI workflows. I prefer a component-driven architecture with strong typing and automated tests.

faq-2.question: Do you build accessible interfaces?
faq-2.answer: Yes. Accessibility (WCAG) is part of my standard delivery: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA where appropriate, and automated/auditory checks during CI. I include accessibility testing in acceptance criteria.

faq-3.question: Can you work with existing design systems or component libraries?
faq-3.answer: Absolutely, it's part of my day job. In production I work with a Tamagui-based design system I've reviewed end to end, and I can adapt components to fit an existing system, extend it safely, or bootstrap a new one (tokens, stories, docs) when it doesn't exist.

faq-4.question: What is your development workflow?
faq-4.answer: Feature-branch Git with small, focused changes, descriptive commits and peer review; CI runs linting, type checks and automated tests, and releases are automated with versioned deployments and changelogs. For larger changes I write spec-first proposals and add quality gates to CI, such as bundle budgets and E2E stability, so quality doesn't depend on discipline alone.

faq-5.question: Do you write tests? What kind?
faq-5.answer: Yes. I write unit and integration tests using Jest and React Testing Library, and add end-to-end tests with Playwright or Cypress for critical flows. Tests are part of the definition of done.

faq-6.question: How do you approach performance optimization?
faq-6.answer: Measure first, optimize second: SSR-first rendering, code-splitting, lazy third-party scripts, image optimization and caching, locked in with performance budgets in CI so regressions can't ship. I verify with lab A/Bs and real-user data (Lighthouse, SpeedCurve) where available; recent production work cut LCP by 23% via an SSR-first rebuild.

faq-7.question: Do you handle SEO and metadata for projects?
faq-7.answer: Yes. For public-facing sites I implement semantic markup, structured data (JSON-LD), proper meta tags and server-side rendering or static rendering strategies for crawlability.

faq-8.question: Are you available for remote work and collaboration?
faq-8.answer: Yes, I collaborate remotely using asynchronous tools (Slack, Notion, Figma, GitHub). I align work with your timezone and team rituals and use frequent check-ins for alignment.

faq-9.question: What is your typical delivery timeline for a medium-sized feature?
faq-9.answer: A medium feature (component + integration + tests + docs) typically takes 2–5 working days, depending on complexity and review cycles. I prioritize incremental delivery so you get working value early.

faq-10.question: How do you handle design handoffs and collaboration with designers?
faq-10.answer: I collaborate closely with designers using Figma: tokens extraction, responsive specs, and component parity. I provide prototypes and work with designers to keep components consistent and maintainable.

faq-11.question: What's it like working with you day-to-day?
faq-11.answer: Async-first and doc-heavy: small, focused changes, honest status updates, and decisions written down with the 'why'. I flag risks early, keep quality gates green so nobody babysits CI, and treat code reviews as teaching moments rather than gatekeeping. Timezones are a solved problem: my current team spans Brazil and Romania.

faq-12.question: What kind of roles and projects are you looking for?
faq-12.answer: I'm currently a full-time frontend engineer on a platform team at Flutter Brazil, working on performance, security and React Native at scale, and always happy to talk about opportunities that fit that profile. Freelance work alongside my job is selective and project-based: best fit is performance engineering, design systems, platform tooling or shipping a React Native (Expo) app from zero.

faq-13.question: How do you price projects or features?
faq-13.answer: Pricing can be hourly or fixed depending on scope. I prefer fixed-price for well-defined scopes and hourly for exploratory work. I always provide a clear proposal breaking down deliverables, milestones and payment terms.

faq-14.question: Can you help with architecture decisions for larger apps?
faq-14.answer: Yes. I help with module boundaries, state and data architecture (Relay vs Apollo included), performance and bundle budgets enforced in CI, and feature-flag rollout strategy, which I apply daily on a multi-team platform codebase.

faq-15.question: Do you contribute to open-source or provide references?
faq-15.answer: I contribute to and maintain open-source projects and can share references or case studies on request. Open-source work demonstrates my coding standards and collaboration style.

faq-16.question: How should I get in touch to discuss a project?
faq-16.answer: The best way is via the contact form below or a direct email. Provide a short brief, your goals, timeline, and any relevant links and I will respond with next steps and availability.

achievements: Owned platform-wide performance, security and quality initiatives across the native apps (Expo/WebView), the web client (Next.js App Router) and shared packages, spanning two teams in seven months.

Cut ~292 KB parsed (~95 KB gzip) from First Load JS by leading the multi-phase bundle-size program: removed an internal devtools bundle from production (−59 KB), code-split Sentry replay (−133 KB parsed) and the error and search screens, and split the app entry into cache-group chunks, locked in as an engineering-wide standard with a CI bundle-size gate.
Removed ~25,000 LOC of dead code in a full web-client sweep: deleted a legacy internal bundling package (−22,240 LOC) plus ~3k LOC of orphan files, unused experiment flags and orphan tests.

Shipped an SSR-first event page with same-build Lighthouse A/B wins on mobile (Slow 4G + 4× CPU): LCP −23% (21.0s → 16.1s), CLS eliminated (0.09 → 0.00), TTI −21% (24.0s → 18.9s) and Speed Index −16%, with the biggest gains on low-end devices (Samsung Galaxy A14).
Reduced home First Contentful Paint from 2.8s → 2.2s (−21%) with a single banner change plus a perceived-loading reduction strategy.

Led security hardening ahead of the 2026 World Cup traffic peak: remediated 40+ dependency CVEs (axios, undici, lodash, node-forge…), added Keycloak token validation to internal APIs, and prevented postMessage XSS across every WebView surface with a centralized hook + a custom ESLint rule, while owning live-match on-call coverage through the traffic peak.

Drove flaky E2E failures from ~10 per submitted change down to near-zero (100% of observed flakiness fixed) by hardening betbuilder, search, events, history/cashout and user-area suites against Mobile Safari cold-start and SSR hydration, changing the team's E2E process to build-first execution.

Unified the new navbar platform-wide behind a feature flag across sportsbook, casino in-game and native with React Native center-label parity, then removed the flag and all legacy navbar wrappers once stable; also shipped the bet-builder rebranding end-to-end.

Delivered the loyalty points experience end to end with an international loyalty team: points UI, 'How to earn' page, exclusive promotions section, chest carousel, full Playwright E2E coverage, Amplitude analytics events and the loyalty-currency rebranding across every locale, while formally on the platform team.

Fixed touch input on every device by building a touch-screen detection hook that removed all breakpoint/user-agent guessing (iPad and touch-screen laptops now correct), and fixed a race condition in the native consent script that rendered raw unstyled HTML inside the apps.

Drove engineering-wide influence: 2 company-wide tech talks (World Cup security hardening; the modern oxlint/oxfmt/tsgo/React Compiler toolchain), onboarded two engineers on feature-flag rollout and the deploy flow, unblocked a company-wide hackathon via an Amplitude fix, and led the discovery for the native home screen, recommending Search as its first native slice.

Achieved 90+ Web Vitals scores and reduced FCP to 0.2s by applying Semantic HTML, SSR, and SEO optimizations across critical pages such as Home, Product, Blog, Catalog, and multiple Landing Pages, significantly improving organic ranking and user experience.
Diagnosed and resolved complex AWS memory leaks, reducing server RAM consumption to under 300MB (<17%), ensuring platform stability even during traffic peaks.
A/B testing implementation with PostHog, enabling data-driven decisions that enhanced user engagement and conversion rates.
Collaborated closely with UX designers to revamp the platform's UI/UX, resulting in a modern, user-friendly interface that boosted user satisfaction and retention.

Designed and implemented a modular, secure checkout system, eliminating fraud risks and integrating a Headless CMS (Hygraph), decentralizing content management and accelerating time-to-market for new features.

Microfrontends and modular architecture experience, enabling independent development and deployment of application components
SaaS product development for diverse clients across various industries
Optimized workflows in public-sector institutions by developing a dynamic PDF reader, reducing download requirements from 1GB to approximately 1MB per page, improving end-user efficiency by 90%.
Managed the evolution of internal methodologies and maintenance of complex projects, working with legacy systems (jQuery / JSF / early React versions) and leading migrations to React 18.
Contributed to accessibility implementation, automated tests, and performance improvements, ensuring long-term sustainability of multi-faceted applications.
A11y audits and improvements across multiple projects
Increased customer retention by 60% by developing a responsive, customizable white-label checkout using Next.js and Chakra UI.
Contributed to an ecosystem of platforms (EdTech, FinTech, Events) responsible for processing over BRL 300 million in annual revenue.

Integrated gateways through Zoop API, including Pix, credit card, and boleto, ensuring secure and efficient payment processing.
Improved application performance by 85%, reducing report response times from 8 seconds to 1.2 seconds through RESTful API optimizations.
Reduced hosting costs by 50% by architecting an efficient monolithic solution using Laravel Mix and React.
Increased operational efficiency by 75% through delivery of a customizable ERP for international management.
Conducted hands-on activities and assisted classes on computer maintenance and assembly, guiding students through practical repairs and builds.
Developed simulators and practical demonstrations to reinforce technical concepts and troubleshooting skills.
